newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Venezuela's national strike said to cost $300 mln.
newsitem.headline: Venezuela's national strike said to cost $300 mln.

text.p: A 12-hour national strike called for Wednesday by Venezuela's unions will cost the economy 1.5 billion bolivars ($300 million), the head of the industrialists' confederation Conindustria was quoted Monday as saying.
Luis Henrique Ball told El Nacional daily newspaper the estimated loss was based on the amount of goods and services that will not be produced during the work stoppage.

Venezuela's umbrella labor organization, the Confederation of Venezuelan Workers (CTV), called the strike last week to protest against delays in promised private sector wage increases and against sharp hikes in gasoline and public services prices.

Key government ministers reiterated at the weekend that the stoppage -- the first one of this magnitude in eight years -- was a legitimate means of pressure by unions to force private employers to raises salaries in accordance with a complex agreement to reform Venezuela's severance payments system.
"Sometimes ... these actions are acceptable as a means of exerting pressure," Finance Minister Luis Raul Matos Azocar said.
Likewise, Planning Minister Teodoro Petkoff said it was "normal for trade unions to express their position through a work stoppage."
Business leaders say that promised wage increases have been granted. Union representatives counter that real wages have not been raised and that only bonuses have been incorporated into salaries.
